entries.title: Isaiah 5:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Now - I will record it to he a witness for God, and against you, as Moses did his song, Deut 31:19 32:1 . To - To the Lord of the vineyard. Of my beloved - Not devised by me, but inspired by God. Vineyard - His church. Hill - Hills being places most commodious for vines.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: He gathered - He removed all hindrances, and gave them all the means of fruitfulness. A tower - For the residence of the keepers.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Nor digged - Vine - dressers use to dig up and open the earth about the roots of the vines. The meaning is, I will remove my ministers, who used great care and diligence to make you fruitful. Thorns - I will give you up to your own lusts. No rain - I will deprive you of all my blessings.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Pleasant - In whom God formerly delighted. A cry - From the oppressed, crying to men for help, and to God for vengeance.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Alone - That they alone may be the lords and owners, and all others only their tenants and servants.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: In mine ears - I heard God speak what I am about to utter.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: One bath - Of wine. The bath contained about eight gallons. Thus an acre did not yield one gallon. An ephah - Which was of the same quantity with the bath, only the bath was the measure of liquid things, the ephah of dry things; and a ephah was the tenth part of an homer. So instead of the increase which that fruitful land commonly yielded, they should loose nine parts of their seed.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The harp - They give up themselves wholly to luxury. The work - What God hath lately done, and is yet doing, and about to do among them; his grievous judgments, partly inflicted, and partly threatened, which required another course of life.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:13
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: No knowledge - No serious consideration of God's works, and of their own duty and danger. Honourable men - Who thought themselves quite out of the reach of famine.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:14
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: And he - That spends all his days in mirth and jollity.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:15
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The mighty - All of them, both high and low, shall be brought to destruction.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Exalted - By the execution of this just judgment. Sanctified - Shall appear to be an holy God, by his righteous judgments.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Then - When God shall have finished that work of judgment. The lambs - The poor and harmless people, who shall be left in the land when the rich are carried into captivity. Manner - Or, by their fold, as this word is manifestly used, Mic 2:12 , the only place of scripture, except this, in which this word is found. Waste places - The lands left by their owners. Fat ones - Of the rich and great men. Strangers - The poor Israelites, who were left to be vine - dressers and husbandmen, 2Kings 25:12 , who are called strangers, because they were so, in reference to that hand, not being the proper owners of it.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:18
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: That draw - That are not only drawn to sin by the allurements of the world; but are active and illustrious in drawing sin to themselves. Cords - Or, with cords of lying, as the last word frequently signifies, with vain and deceitful arguments and pretences, whereby sinners generally draw themselves to sin. A rope - With all their might, as beasts commonly do that draw carts with ropes.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:19
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Let him - God, in whose name thou and other prophets are always threatening us. This was the plain language of their actions; they lived as if they were of this opinion. The Holy One - They scornfully repeated the title usually given by the prophets to God.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:20
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: To them - That take away the difference between good and evil; that justify wicked men and things, and condemn piety, or righteous persons.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:22
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: To mingle - To drink: the antecedent being put for the consequent: for they mingled it in order to drinking.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:23
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Take away - Pronounce sentence against him.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:24
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Rottenness - They shall be like a tree which not only withers in its branches, but dies and rots at the roots, therefore is past recovery. Dust - Shall be resolved into dust, and yield no fruit.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:26
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: An ensign - To call them together for his service. From far - To the Chaldeans; for even Babylon is called a far country, chap. 39:3 . And he saith nations, because the Chaldean army was made up of several nations. Will hiss - Or, will whistle unto, or for them: will gather them together by his word. as shepherds gather their sheep. He intimates how easily and speedily God can do this work. From the ends - Which is not to be understood strictly, but with a latitude, from very remote places.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:27
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Nor sleep - They shall all be watchful and diligent to take all opportunities of executing my judgments. Nor latchet - I will take all impediments out of their way.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:28
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Bent - Who are every way furnished and ready for my work, waiting only for my command. Flint - Because they shall not be broken or battered by the length or stonyness and ruggedness of the way. Whirlwind - For the swiftness of their march, and for the force and violence of their chariots in battle.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:29
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Roar - Which signifies both their cruelty, and their eagerness to devour the prey.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:30
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Sorrow - Darkness; that is, sorrow; the latter word explains the former. The heavens - When they look up to the heavens, as men in distress usually do, they see no light there.
